summary: This document defines Mobile IP Agent Advertisement and Registration Request extensions that let a foreign agent challenge a mobile node, giving replay protection and allowing methods such as CHAP. It also adds a Mobile-AAA Authentication extension so a node can supply credentials through AAA infrastructure. It replaces RFC 3012 and updates RFC 3344.

eli5.summary: A guest arriving in a new town is asked a fresh question by the host to prove who they are, so someone can't reuse an old answer. It also lets the host check credentials with a central office.

questions: what is the mobile ip challenge extension
how does mobile ip prevent replay attacks
what is the mobile aaa authentication extension
what is challenge window in mobile ip
subtitle: How a Mobile IPv4 foreign agent hands out fresh challenges so a visiting device cannot replay an old registration.

tldr.problem: In Mobile IP, the Mobile-Foreign Authentication extension gives a foreign agent no direct guarantee against replayed registrations, and it cannot use existing techniques such as CHAP to authenticate portable computers.
tldr.mechanism: The foreign agent puts a random Challenge extension in its Agent Advertisements and Registration Replies. The mobile node echoes it in a Mobile-Foreign Challenge extension, followed by an authentication extension, including a new Mobile-AAA Authentication extension for AAA infrastructure.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4721 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 3012 and updates RFC 3344. It adds error codes, a tracking rule for used challenges and a clearer treatment of the AAA extension.

today: RFC 4721 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2007. It obsoletes RFC 3012 and updates RFC 3344, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Replay Problem in Mobile IP
sections.content:
Mobile IP lets a mobile node keep working as it moves between networks. On a visited network it may register through a foreign agent. The base specification, RFC 3344, defines a Mobile-Foreign Authentication extension so the node can authenticate itself to that agent.

RFC 4721 points out two weaknesses. That extension gives the foreign agent no direct guarantee that the protocol is protected from replays, and it does not allow existing techniques such as CHAP (RFC 1994) to authenticate portable computers.

The fix has two parts: a challenge/response mechanism carried in Agent Advertisements and Registration Requests, and a new Mobile-AAA Authentication extension that lets a node supply credentials for authorization through common AAA infrastructure. The foreign agent may talk to that infrastructure with protocols outside the scope of this document.
sections.eli5: A copied password can be used again by a thief. The fix is to make the visited network pick a new secret word every time, so an old copy is useless.

sections.title: The Agent Advertisement Challenge
sections.content:
The foreign agent inserts a Challenge extension into its Agent Advertisements. It carries a previously unused random value that the mobile node can use to compute authentication for its next Registration Request. The extension has type 24, a length, and a challenge value that SHOULD be at least 32 bits. RFC 4086 is cited for generating suitable pseudo-random values.

A foreign agent may answer a Router Solicitation with a multicast or a unicast advertisement. For a multicast one it MUST NOT generate a new challenge and must re-use the most recent of the CHALLENGE_WINDOW advertised values. For a unicast one, it SHOULD repeat the challenge last sent to that node if that challenge has not been used; otherwise it MUST generate and remember a new one.
sections.eli5: The visited network writes a fresh random number on a card and shows it to every newcomer. If you ask for the card again before using it, you get the same card. Once it is used, you get a new one.

sections.title: How Registration Works with Challenges
sections.content:
If the Agent Advertisement has a Challenge extension and the mobile node has no security association with the foreign agent, the node MUST include the challenge in a Mobile-Foreign Challenge extension and MUST also include a Mobile-AAA Authentication extension. If it does have a security association, it SHOULD include the challenge and MUST include a Mobile-Foreign Authentication extension, which MUST follow the Challenge extension.

The foreign agent checks that the challenge is unused by that node. A missing challenge earns a reply with code missing_challenge; a reused one SHOULD get stale_challenge; one that was not recently advertised SHOULD get unknown_challenge. The agent MUST NOT accept any challenge outside the last CHALLENGE_WINDOW values, and it MUST silently discard a request that has a Challenge extension but no Mobile-Foreign or Mobile-AAA Authentication extension.

The foreign agent SHOULD include a new challenge in any Registration Reply, successful or not, so the node can register again without waiting for an advertisement. The home agent, if it recognizes the Challenge extension, MUST echo it in its reply. Its type falls in the range 128-255, so a home agent that does not recognize it MUST still process the request. After any error, a node that registers again MUST use a new challenge.

A node using a co-located care-of address registering directly with its home agent MUST NOT include the Mobile-Foreign Challenge extension; replay protection then comes from the Identification field defined in RFC 3344.
sections.eli5: You show the desk the card number along with your proof. If you forgot the number, used an old one, or made one up, the desk tells you which mistake you made. After each visit the desk hands you a new card.

sections.title: The Extensions on the Wire
sections.content:
Two Challenge extensions exist. The one in advertisements has type 24. The Mobile-Foreign Challenge extension in Registration Requests has type 132 (skippable) and copies the challenge value it received.

The Generalized Mobile IP Authentication extension has type 36 (not skippable) and fields Subtype, Length, SPI and Authenticator. Length is 4 plus the number of octets in the Authenticator and MUST be at least 20. Only one subtype is defined here: subtype 1, the Mobile-AAA Authentication subtype.

By default the Mobile-AAA authenticator is HMAC-MD5 computed over the preceding Mobile IP data followed by the Type, Subtype, Length and SPI. Every mobile node MUST be able to produce it. If both the Mobile-AAA and Mobile-Foreign Authentication extensions are present, the Mobile-AAA one MUST come first, and the Mobile-Home Authentication extension MUST appear before the Mobile-AAA one.
sections.eli5: The challenge card and the proof each go in their own labelled envelope. The labels tell the reader what is inside and in what order to open them.

sections.title: SPIs and the RADIUS-Style Authenticator
sections.content:
Authentication extensions carry a Security Parameters Index (SPI) that selects a security association. Values 0-255 are reserved for special use, with the list kept by IANA.

Some AAA servers admit only a single security association, so they cannot use the SPI to pick one. For them, the reserved SPI CHAP_SPI selects the CHAP-style procedure used by many RADIUS servers (RFC 2865). The authenticator is an MD5 hash over the high-order octet of the challenge, the key, an MD5 of the preceding Mobile IP data and extension header fields, and the least significant 237 octets of the challenge. The inner hash exists because RADIUS cannot carry attributes longer than 253 octets.

With a co-located care-of address the challenge value 0 is used in this computation.
sections.eli5: Some offices only know one secret handshake. For them there is a special code that means use that handshake, mixing in the challenge card.

sections.title: Parameters and Error Codes
sections.content:
Agents SHOULD be able to configure two parameters. CHALLENGE_WINDOW defaults to 2 and SHOULD be at least 2, which makes it much less likely that a node registers with a challenge outside the set the foreign agent allows. CHAP_SPI defaults to 2.

Seven error values are listed for Registration Replies, shown in the table below. Three of them (fa_bad_aaa_auth, ha_bad_aaa_auth and ha_wrong_challenge) are new in this document, and ha_wrong_challenge may appear in the Status field of the FA Error extension from RFC 4636. Code 67 already existed.

To avoid tracking every old challenge, the foreign agent can keep challenges in advertisement order. Nodes MUST NOT use a challenge advertised before the last one they used. An appendix gives pseudo-code for this.
sections.eli5: The desk keeps only the last couple of cards on hand. Each kind of mistake has its own number so the visitor knows what went wrong.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
A replayed authenticator for an old challenge is caught because the foreign agent checks whether it recently advertised that challenge. Different nodes using the same challenge value is not a vulnerability, since the authentication data covers other data, at least the node's own IP address. A challenge shorter than 4 octets calls for the agent to also record the Identification field.

The RADIUS-style MD5 method is less secure than HMAC-MD5 and MUST be avoided whenever possible.

An attacker could flood the foreign agent with solicitations or bogus requests so that fresh challenges keep invalidating the one a node is trying to use. To prevent this, the foreign agent MUST NOT invalidate previously unused challenges when answering unauthenticated requests, and MUST NOT allocate new storage for them.
sections.eli5: A pest could keep asking for new cards so your card never works. So the desk is told not to throw away unused cards or buy new storage just because a stranger asks.

sections.title: Changes Since RFC 3012
sections.content:
Appendix A lists what changed from the original RFC 3012. Among the changes: the foreign agent is recommended to put a challenge in every Registration Reply, and it MUST record the challenge values each node has used. Nodes are forbidden to use challenges advertised before the last one they used.

The revision also adds the fa_bad_aaa_auth, ha_bad_aaa_auth and ha_wrong_challenge error codes, clarifies how foreign and home agents process the Mobile-AAA extension, and allows that extension with a co-located care-of address.
sections.eli5: This is the second edition of the rulebook. The new edition fixes confusing parts, adds more error messages and makes the card rules stricter.
